title: Sandboxed swallowback notebook — escalation ladder & tiny experiments
content:
Context:
- Weekend low-handoff deploys need a tiny, repeatable cookbook for fast swallowbacks that don't require a full incident page. This is a personal scratchpad for the micro-procedures and a few small experiments to validate the ladder.

Goals (short):
1) Give on-call a 5-step ladder they can follow in < 8 minutes to safely reduce blast radius.
2) Provide a tiny simulation harness (load + latency bump) to exercise the ladder in staging.
3) Capture useful thresholds and commands that are easily copy-pasteable.

Assumptions:
- We deploy with model-version pinned via config-service; pin/unpin can be done with:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/text/generate","pin":"model-v2.3.1"}' https://api.redwood.dev/admin/pin
- Canary cohorts are 0.5% and 5% in prod for weekend experiments; we have warmup caches on the dedicated pool.
- Observable signals: client-side error_rate, infra error_rate (5xx), 95th/99th latency, token-cost per request, eviction-rate from LRU KVC.

Quick escalation ladder (targets for first 8 minutes):
Step 0 (preflight, before touching traffic)
- Confirm rollout window and responder availability (bookmarked on-call name).
- Post short note in #deploy-announce with link to this doc and GH PR.
- Sanity check: staging pass + smoke: 10 requests/s for 10m, < 10% tail latency change vs baseline.

Step 1: Canary watch (0–10 minutes)
- Watch: infra 5xx > 0.3% absolute OR client-facing error_rate increase > 0.5% OR 95th latency increase > 25% relative -> go to step 2.
- If metrics stay within limits for 10m, increment cohort to next bucket.

Step 2: Pinback to safe variant (quick rollback)
- If threshold hit, attempt soft pin: route canary cohort back to previous model-variant via API (example):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/text/generate","pin":"model-v2.3.0"}' https://api.redwood.dev/admin/pin
- Expected outcome: immediate reduction in error spike (minutes). Monitor for 3m then decide full rollback.

Step 3: Cohort siphon & warmup fallback
- If pinback doesn't help, siphon remaining cohorts to warm baseline instances: set routing policy to prefer region/hardware variant with known-good quantization.
- Command (example): update routing policy via console -> \"prefer: baseline-pool\". If CLI: redwood route update --route /text/generate --prefer baseline-pool

Step 4: Full rollback + incident note
- If system still degraded after 10m post-pinback, flip traffic fully and file short incident stub (title + timeline + what we did) in Linear. Tag the release owner and SRE.
- Full rollback command: redwood rollout rollback --release 2025-01-10-09-22 

Step 5: Postmortem triage checklist (on return)
- Capture top 5 request traces, sample prompt sets that regressed, and token cost variance.
- Reproduce in staging with a spike script that matches production tail.

Tiny experiments to run in staging (lab things)
- E1: 25% latency injection at target backends to validate evacuation sequence. Measure recovery time for each ladder step.
  - script: siege-style ramp to 500r/s with artificial 200ms added to GPU kernel.
- E2: Small cache priming vs cold start: compare user cohorts with/without prefix-KV cache.
- E3: Pin flip speed: measure median time for pin change to propagate and for obs metrics to reflect. Aim < 60s to observe stabilizing delta.

Monitoring knobs and thresholds (notes):
- 5xx infra threshold: 0.3% absolute over rolling 5m -> alert to pager.
- client error threshold: +0.5% absolute over baseline (rolling 5m) -> page.
- latency: 95th > 25% relative vs 1h baseline -> bring to lead.
- token-cost-per-request uplift: +12% -> block increase and examine quantization path.

Checklist for a quiet deploy (preflight):
- [ ] Confirm fallback image is signed and present in artifact registry.
- [ ] Notify SRE and list on-call who can accept a page.
- [ ] Run quick load test: 2m at expected steady QPS, check dispatch latencies.
- [ ] Confirm canary config exists and is set to 0.5% initially.
- [ ] Add 2 synthetic monitors in Datadog for specific prompt templates.
- [ ] Share link to smoke perf dashboard in the deploy message.

Notes-to-self / gotchas spotted previously:
- Pin API has ~30–90s propagation variance (need better instrumentation).
- Cold-starts for quantized kernels sometimes produce transient tail latency spikes after a pin. Consider a small pre-warm migration step (shadow load a 1% traffic path to new variant before switching).
- Watch for request fanout in user clients (some clients retry aggressively, amplifies error signals).

Follow-ups to schedule:
- Add a tiny synthetic that hits the kv-cache-sensitive prompt set every 2m in staging (owner: Maya).
- Measure pin API RTT distribution and log to console (owner: Liam).
- Run E1/E3 back to back this sprint and capture recovery graphs (owner: me).

Rough TL;DR to paste into deploy Slack: \"Brief weekend deploy checklist + 5-step swallowback ladder. If you see >0.3% 5xx or +0.5% client errors, perform soft pin to previous model variant, monitor 3m, then escalate to siphon or full rollback. Staging experiments are in this doc. Samir.\"

Unresolved questions:
- Do we want an automated soft-pin rule (platform) when 95th latency crosses X? Automation could reduce human time but may hide root cause.
- What's the minimum cohort size where pinback is reliable vs noisy? 0.5% is experimental.

End of notebook — quick incremental edits welcome.
__notes: personal scratchpad: intentionally informal, not final runbook
